decisions.reason: The pegboard shelf display is a small variation on the firm's core cardboard competence, so its own R&D and design staff can keep absorbing feedback and adapting it, even though it no longer has its own web page.
The standard quarter-pallet display is a core format that builds directly on existing knowledge and capacity, so it can be kept within the general range despite its lower web visibility.
The eighth-pallet format applies familiar expertise to smaller placements, so it stays easy to interpret and improve and is worth keeping.

Wood lies outside the firm's paper-based knowledge base, which limits its ability to learn from results, and the missing web presence suggests weak traction, so resources are better spent on the core business.

Although it uses familiar cardboard know-how, the media segment is shrinking and the product has disappeared from view, so freeing its resources for core displays and new development makes more sense.
